subject: history
title: Interpretations: Why Historians Disagree
welcome_lead: Today you'll stretch — explain why historians disagree and how to write about it.
meta_desc: GCSE History stretch — interpretations, why historians disagree, how to write top answers.
final_note: You can now explain why historians disagree and write a strong interpretation answer.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Three big reasons: different evidence, different questions, different times.

Historians select different sources and place different emphasis. A 1950s writer on WWII has different access from one in 2020.

Hindsight can sharpen judgement but also distort it.

Historians writing in 1945 saw the Cold War only just beginning. By 1991 they could weigh its whole arc. Both views have value — but the questions they ask differ.

For top marks: identify the interpretation, explain it, use your own knowledge to support or challenge it, and weigh it against other views.

Use the framework: 'This historian argues X because. However, others stress Y.' Don't just describe — judge.

mcqs.q: Did Gorbachev intend to dissolve the Soviet Union?
options: Gorbachev dissolved the USSR by signing a treaty with Ronald Reagan.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
Gorbachev took power planning to abolish communism and dissolve the USSR.
No — he wanted to reform and save Soviet socialism; glasnost and perestroika unleashed forces (nationalism, economic chaos) he could not control.
